question: A dealer runs a scheme offering 'buy 5 items and get 2 items free'. Each item is priced at ₹250. What is the total discount amount for a customer buying under this scheme?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a 'Buy X Get Y Free' scheme, the actual discount amount given to the customer is strictly the total marked price of the free items.

Number of free items = 2

Marked Price per item = ₹250

Total Discount Amount = 2 × 250 = ₹500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Paid items = 5

Free items = 2

Marked Price (MP) per item = ₹250

**Formula Used:**

Total MP = Total items × MP per item

Total Selling Price (SP) = Paid items × MP per item

Discount Amount = Total MP − Total SP

 Total MP = 7 × 250 = ₹1750
 Customer pays = 5 × 250 = ₹1250
 Discount Amount = 1750 − 1250 = ₹500

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total items taken by customer = 5 + 2 = 7

⇒ Total MP of 7 items = 7 × 250 = ₹1750

⇒ Total SP (since customer only pays for 5 items) = 5 × 250 = ₹1250

⇒ Discount Amount = Total MP − Total SP

⇒ Discount Amount = 1750 − 1250 = ₹500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Buy X Get Y Free %

To calculate the actual percentage discount equivalent to the scheme: Discount % = [Free Items ÷ (Paid + Free Items)] × 100.

Marked Price (MP)

The labeled or written price of an article. Any discount or scheme offered by the seller is always calculated on the MP, not the Cost Price (CP).

Successive Discounts

When two successive discounts of d₁% and d₂% are given, the effective single discount is calculated as (d₁ + d₂ − d₁×d₂/100)%.
